Rashi on Niddah 40a:10:1.english: The law of the woman who gives birth - It implies [that there is] one law for a woman who gives birth to many offspring.

Rashi on Niddah 40a:12:1.hebrew: שלפני מלאת - ילדה עכשיו וילדה לאחר שמונים, קמא הוי לפני מלאת, ובתרא הוי לאחר מלאת:
Rashi on Niddah 40a:12:1.english: That is before completion - [If] she gave birth now and gave birth [again] after eighty [days], the first is before completion, and the latter is after completion.

Rashi on Niddah 40a:12:2.hebrew: זאת - משמע כמו שמפורש בענין, קרבן אחד לולד אחד:
Rashi on Niddah 40a:12:2.english: This - It implies, as is specified in the passage, one offering for one offspring.

Rashi on Niddah 40a:12:3.english: This applies - That she does not bring a single offering for [a birth] before the completion [of her days of purity] and [a birth] after the completion.

Rashi on Niddah 40a:13:1.hebrew: בתרי עיבורי - שילדה וחזרה ונתעברה בתוך ימי טוהר, וילדה לאחר שמונים:
Rashi on Niddah 40a:13:1.english: In two pregnancies - Where she gave birth, and then conceived again within the days of purity, and gave birth after eighty [days].

Rashi on Niddah 40a:13:2.english: Such as Yehuda and Ḥizkiyya - As we say in [chapter] HaMapelet (above, Niddah 27a), that the latter [twin] was delayed after the first by three months.

Rashi on Niddah 40a:14:1.english: Rabbi Shimon concedes - With regard to [an animal born by] caesarean section.

Rashi on Niddah 40a:14:2.hebrew: שאינו קדוש - קדושת הגוף, אלא כשאר קדשים שקדם מומן להקדשן, דלא קדשי אלא כעצים וכאבנים לדמיהם, ויוצאין לחולין ליגזוז וליעבד:
Rashi on Niddah 40a:14:2.english: That it is not consecrated - [With] bodily sanctity, but rather like other consecrated animals whose blemish preceded their consecration, which are consecrated only like wood and stones for their monetary value, and go out to unconsecrated status to be sheared and to be worked.

Rashi on Niddah 40a:14:3.hebrew: לידה לידה - כתיב בקדשים (ויקרא כ״ב:כ״ז) שור או כשב או עז כי יולד, וכתיב בבכור (דברים ט״ו:י״ט) אשר יולד:
Rashi on Niddah 40a:14:3.english: "Birth," "birth" - It is written regarding consecrated [animals] (Leviticus 22:27): "An ox, or a sheep, or a goat, when it is born," and it is written regarding a firstborn (Deuteronomy 15:19): "that is born."

Rashi on Niddah 40a:15:1.hebrew: מאדם - לענין טומאה וטהרה, דכתיב: וילדה זכר:
Rashi on Niddah 40a:15:1.english: From a person - With regard to ritual impurity and purity, as it is written: "and gives birth to a male."

Rashi on Niddah 40a:16:1.hebrew: אמו מאמו - בבכור כתיב (שמות כב) שבעת ימים יהיה עם אמו, ובקדשים כתיב (ויקרא כב) והיה שבעת ימים תחת אמו:
Rashi on Niddah 40a:16:1.english: Its mother from its mother - Regarding a firstborn, it is written (Exodus 22): "Seven days it shall be with its mother," and regarding consecrated animals, it is written (Leviticus 22): "And it shall be seven days under its mother."

Rashi on Niddah 40a:17:1.hebrew: שכן אם בהמת קדשים פיגול נותר וטמא - אם: בתרוייהו כתיב אמו, ותרוייהו בהמת קדשים, ופגול ונותר וטמא נוהג בהם, לאפוקי אדם דליתיה בכל הני:
Rashi on Niddah 40a:17:1.english: For "mother," sacrificial animal, piggul, notar, and ritually impure - "Mother": In both of them it is written "its mother"; and both of them are sacrificial animals; and piggul, notar, and ritual impurity apply to them — to the exclusion of a human, who is not subject to any of these.

Rashi on Niddah 40a:18:1.hebrew: פשוט - אדם משתעי בין בפשוט בין בבכור, וכן קדשים הוו פשוטים. ובין באדם ובין בקדשים לא משתעו בזכרים לחודייהו טפי מבנקבות, לאפוקי בכור דליתיה אלא בזכרים. ותרוייהו, בין אדם בין קדשים, לא הוו קדושין מאליהם, אבל בכור קדושתו מאליו. ובין קדשים ובין אדם לא הוו מתנות כהונה, כגון שלמים לבעלים הן, לאפוקי בכור דהוי ממתנות כהונה:
Rashi on Niddah 40a:18:1.english: Ordinary - [The passage concerning] a human speaks both of an ordinary [child] and of a firstborn, and likewise sacrificial animals are ordinary [offspring]. And both regarding a human and regarding sacrificial animals, [the verses] do not speak of males alone any more than of females, to the exclusion of a firstborn, which applies only to males. And both of them, whether a human or sacrificial animals, do not become sacred on their own, whereas a firstborn's sanctity is of itself. And neither sacrificial animals nor a human are gifts of the priesthood — for example, peace-offerings belong to the owners — to the exclusion of a firstborn, which is among the gifts of the priesthood.

Rashi on Niddah 40a:19:1.english: Which supports Rabbi Yoḥanan - Who said that Rabbi Shimon concedes regarding [an animal born by] caesarean section of consecrated animals.

Rashi on Niddah 40a:19:2.hebrew: זאת תורת העולה היא העולה - ומהאי קרא נפקא לן בזבחים (דף כז:) פסולין שאם עלו לא ירדו, דכתיב: על מוקדה, משתעלה תוקד. וכתב רחמנא זאת, דמשמע מיעוטא, כלומר: זאת אם עלתה לא תרד, אבל אחרת, אע"פ שעלתה, תרד. וכתיב היא, דמשמע מיעוטא. וכתיב העולה, דמשמע העולה - עולה כשרה ולא פסולה. והני תלתא מיעוטי ממעטי הני תלתא פסולי:
Rashi on Niddah 40a:19:2.english: This is the law of the burnt offering; it is the burnt offering - And from this verse we derive in Zevachim (page 27b) [the rule concerning] disqualified [sacrifices] that if they ascended [the altar], they do not descend, as it is written: "Upon its pyre" — once it has ascended, it shall burn. And the Merciful One wrote "This" [zot], which indicates an exclusion, that is to say: this one, if it ascended, shall not descend, but another, even though it ascended, shall descend. And it is written "It is" [hi], which indicates an exclusion. And it is written "The burnt offering" [ha'olah], which indicates "the burnt offering" — a fit burnt offering, and not a disqualified one. And these three exclusions exclude these three [cases of] disqualified offerings:

Rashi on Niddah 40a:1:1.hebrew: יוצא דופן - על ידי סם נפתחו מעיה, והוציאו את העובר לחוץ, ונתרפאת:
Rashi on Niddah 40a:1:1.english: [An offspring] that emerges through the [abdominal] wall - By means of a drug, her abdomen was opened, and they brought the fetus out, and she healed.

Rashi on Niddah 40a:2:1.english: All women - With regard to a menstruant [niddah].

Rashi on Niddah 40a:2:2.hebrew: מטמאות - מכי אתא דם לבית החיצון, אע"ג דהעמידוהו כותלי רחמה:
Rashi on Niddah 40a:2:2.english: Become impure - From when the blood reaches the outer chamber, even though the walls of her womb held it back.

Rashi on Niddah 40a:2:3.english: In her flesh - This implies inside her flesh.

Rashi on Niddah 40a:2:4.english: Outside - In the Gemara, [it] derives this.

Rashi on Niddah 40a:3:1.english: That his limbs shuddered - Semen was dislodged from his body.

Rashi on Niddah 40a:5:1.hebrew: אלא כעין שהזריעה - כגון נימוק הולד, כדאמר בהמפלת (לעיל נדה כו.): שליא בבית, הבית טמא כו', רבי שמעון אומר: הולד נימוק. ואמר בגמרא: מודה רבי שמעון שאמו טמאה לידה, ויליף טעמא מהכא. אבל רבנן לא צריך להו קרא להכי, דהא לדידהו כיון דאמרי הבית טמא לית להו נימוק, ופשיטא דאמו טמאה לידה:
Rashi on Niddah 40a:5:1.english: Only resembling that which she emitted - For example, where the fetus dissolved, as it says in [chapter] HaMapelet (above, Niddah 26a): "[If there is] an afterbirth in a house, the house is impure, etc.; Rabbi Shimon says: The fetus dissolved." And it says in the Gemara: Rabbi Shimon concedes that its mother is impure [with the impurity of] childbirth, and he derives the reason from here. However, the Rabbis do not need a verse for this, for according to them, since they say "the house is impure," they do not hold [that the fetus] dissolved, and it is obvious that its mother is impure [with the impurity of] childbirth.

Rashi on Niddah 40a:6:1.hebrew: תלד - ואם נקבה תלד, דמצי למכתב ואם נקבה וטמאה שבועים:
Rashi on Niddah 40a:6:1.english: She gives birth - [In the verse:] "And if she gives birth to a female," for it could have written: "And if a female, she shall be unclean two weeks."

Rashi on Niddah 40a:9:1.hebrew: לחייב על כל בן ובן - שאם טבלה לאחר י"ד לנקבה, ושמשה, ונתעברה, וילדה לאחר שמונים, מביאה שני קרבנות:
Rashi on Niddah 40a:9:1.english: To obligate for each and every son - That if she immersed after fourteen [days] for a female, and engaged in relations, and conceived, and gave birth after eighty [days], she brings two offerings.

Tosafot on Niddah 40a:14:1.hebrew: מודה ר"ש בקדשים שאינו קדוש - בפ' בתרא דבכורות (דף נז:), גבי ר"א ברבי יהודה דאית ליה יוצא דופן קדוש, אמר: סבר לה כר"ש, דאמר יוצא דופן ולד מעליא הוא. ותימה, דהא ר"ש מודה דבקדשים אינו קדוש, כדאמר רבי יוחנן הכא, וכדמוכח נמי בברייתא דמייתי בסמוך. וי"ל, דסבר כר"ש ועדיפא מדר"ש, דאפילו בקדשים קאמר דקדוש:
Tosafot on Niddah 40a:14:1.english: Rabbi Shimon concedes regarding consecrated [animals] that it is not consecrated - In the last chapter of Bekhorot (57b), regarding Rabbi Elazar ben Rabbi Yehuda, who maintains that [an animal born by] caesarean section (yotzei dofen) is consecrated, [the Gemara] states: He holds in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, who says [that an offspring born by] caesarean section is a full-fledged offspring. And [this is] perplexing, for behold, Rabbi Shimon concedes that regarding consecrated [animals] it is not consecrated, as Rabbi Yoḥanan says here, and as is also proved in the baraita that is brought nearby. And one can say that he holds in accordance with Rabbi Shimon, and goes beyond Rabbi Shimon, for he maintains that even regarding consecrated [animals] it is consecrated.

Tosafot on Niddah 40a:14:2.hebrew: גמר לידה לידה מבכור - בפ' ולד חטאת (מעילה דף יג.) במעילה, גבי ולד המעושרת לא ינק מן המעושרת, יליף אמו אמו מבכור; והכל אחד, כדמוכח בשמעתין. וא"ת, דבפרק מרובה (ב"ק דף עז:) אמר: כל מקום שנאמר שה אינו אלא להוציא את הכלאים; וקאמר: למעוטי מאי? אי למעוטי קדשים — בהדיא כתיב בהו או כשב, פרט לכלאים; אם למעשר — תחת תחת יליף מקדשים; ואי לבכור — העברה העברה יליף ממעשר. והשתא, אמאי אצטריך למילף בכור ממעשר, ומעשר גופיה ילפינן מקדשים? הוה ליה למימר דנילף בכור לידה לידה או אמו אמו מקדשים! וי"ל, דלא ילפינן לידה לידה או אמו אמו אלא כגון הכא דאיירי בלידה, או במעילה דאיירי בענין אמהות. וא"ת, ובשמעתין אמאי צריך ג"ש דלידה לידה או אמו אמו? נילף פסול יוצא דופן בקדשים מג"ש דתחת ממעשר, ומעשר מג"ש דהעברה מבכור! וי"ל, דג"ש דלידה ודאמו צריך לשום דרשה אחריתי:
Tosafot on Niddah 40a:14:2.english: He derives "birth" "birth" from a firstborn - In the chapter [entitled] "Velad Chatat" (Meilah 13a), in [tractate] Meilah, regarding "the offspring of a tithed animal shall not suckle from a tithed animal", it derives [by verbal analogy] "its mother" "its mother" from a firstborn; and it is all one [and the same derivation], as is evident in our sugya. And if you say that in chapter Merubah (Bava Kamma 77b), [the Gemara] states: "Wherever 'a lamb' is stated, it serves only to exclude a hybrid [kilayim]"; and it says: "To exclude what? If to exclude consecrated animals, it is explicitly written regarding them: 'or a sheep' [Leviticus 22:27] — to exclude a hybrid; if [to exclude animal] tithe, it derives [this by verbal analogy of] 'under' 'under' from consecrated animals; and if [to exclude] a firstborn, it derives [this by verbal analogy of] 'passing' 'passing' from tithe." And now, why was it necessary to derive a firstborn from tithe, when tithe itself we derive from consecrated animals? It should have said that we derive a firstborn [by verbal analogy of] "birth" "birth" or "its mother" "its mother" from consecrated animals! And one can answer that we do not derive [laws via the verbal analogy of] "birth" "birth" or "its mother" "its mother" except [in cases] such as here, which deals with birth, or in Meilah, which deals with the matter of mothers. And if you say: But in our sugya, why is the verbal analogy of "birth" "birth" or "its mother" "its mother" needed? Let us derive the disqualification of a caesarean-born [animal] in consecrated animals from the verbal analogy of "under" from tithe, and [that of] tithe from the verbal analogy of "passing" from a firstborn! And one can answer that the verbal analogy of "birth" and of "its mother" is needed for another exposition.

Tosafot on Niddah 40a:18:1.hebrew: הנך נפישין - וא"ת, דבפרק יש בכור (בכורות דף מז:) אר"ש דיוצא דופן בכור לנחלה הוי, דיליף מוילדו לו בנים לידה לידה מאשה, דאית ליה הכא דהוי ולד; והשתא, לילף מבכור בהמה, שכן בכור, זכר (מתנות)? וי"ל, דאדם מאדם עדיף, שכן אין שייך בהו פגול, נותר וטמא, דאינו קדשים, ושייך בהו טומאה וטהרה. ובפרק ראשית הגז (חולין דף קלז.) דקאמר פשוט מפשוט עדיף, אע"ג דהנהו נפישי — התם משום דהוי בהמה מבהמה; אבל הכא דבהמה מאדם, לא:
Tosafot on Niddah 40a:18:1.english: These are more numerous - And if you say that in the chapter [entitled] "Yesh Bekhor" (Bekhorot 47b), Rabbi Shimon said that [one born by] caesarean section is a firstborn with respect to inheritance, as he derives [this] from "and they have borne him sons" (Deuteronomy 21:15) [via a verbal analogy of] "giving birth" (leidah) / "giving birth" (leidah) from a woman [giving birth], for he maintains here that [a caesarean birth] is considered an offspring; and now, let him derive [it] from a firstborn animal, as [they share the characteristics of being] a firstborn [and] a male, (gifts)? And one can say that [deriving] a human from a human is preferable, as [the disqualifications of] piggul [improper sacrificial intent], notar [remnant], and tamei [sacrificial impurity] do not apply to them, since [humans] are not sacrificial offerings; and [the laws of] ritual impurity and purity do apply to them. And [as for that which] in the chapter [entitled] "Reishit HaGez" (Chullin 137a), it says that [deriving] an ordinary [case] from an ordinary [case] is preferable, even though those [characteristics shared with a firstborn] are more numerous — there [in Chullin], it is because it is [deriving] an animal from an animal; but here [in Niddah], where it is [deriving] an animal from a human, no [it does not override the greater number of shared characteristics].

Tosafot on Niddah 40a:19:1.hebrew: זאת היא העולה - הכי כתיב קרא: זאת תורת העולה היא העולה. הרי ג' מיעוטי: זאת, והיא, וה' דהעולה תנינא; דהעולה קמא דריש רבא בתמיד נשחט (פסחים נח:): העולה, עולה ראשונה. מהני ג' מיעוטי ממעט הנך, ומתורת מרבינן אינך פסולין דאם עלו לא ירדו כר"ש. וא"ת: והא ר' יהודה סבר בפ"ק דזבחים (דף כד) דרצפה מקדשת כמזבח, ואם כן כולם יעלו, והיכי משכחת פסול בכל הנהו לבר מהני ג' כיון דאם עלו לא ירדו? וי"ל: כגון שיש הפסק בין הבהמה לרצפת עזרה. ואם תאמר: והיכי ממעט הני ג' פסולי? הא צריך חד מיעוט לרובע ונרבע ולכל הנהו דמודה רבי שמעון בהו דאם עלו ירדו! וי"ל: דנשחטה בלילה ויצא דמה ממעט תרוייהו מחד מיעוטא, דשקולים הם. וא"ת: קדשי קדשים ששחטן בדרום, דאמר בריש מעילה (דף ב:) דאליבא דר' יהודה כ"ע ל"פ דתרד, אמאי? הא ליכא מיעוטא רביעית! ולר"ש נמי, לרבא דאמר תרד, הא פסולן בקדש הוא, דהא אית ליה הכשר בקדשים קלים דכשרים בדרום, כמו שאפרש, דהיכא דאית ליה הכשר בעלמא איקרו פסולן בקדש! וי"ל: דשחיטה בדרום הוי כעין שחיטת חוץ, וכמו דחנקינהו דמי, כדקאמר התם לר"ש:
Tosafot on Niddah 40a:19:1.english: This is the burnt offering - This is how the verse is written: "This is the law of the burnt offering; that is the burnt offering" (Leviticus 6:2). Behold, [there are] three exclusions: "This" (zot), and "that" (hi), and the [letter] heh of the second [mention of] "the burnt offering" (ha-olah); for the first [mention of] "the burnt offering," Rava expounds in [the chapter] "Tamid Nishchat" (Pesachim 58b): "The burnt offering" — the first burnt offering. From these three exclusions [the baraita] excludes those [three disqualified offerings: one slaughtered at night, one whose blood spilled, and one whose blood went outside the courtyard curtains, such that if they ascended the altar, they must descend], and from "the law of" (torat) we include the other disqualified [offerings], that if they ascended, they do not descend, in accordance with Rabbi Shimon. And if you say: But does not Rabbi Yehuda maintain in the first chapter of Zevachim (daf 24a) that the pavement [of the Temple courtyard] sanctifies like the altar? And if so, all of them should ascend! And how do you find disqualification among all of those [offerings], other than these three, since if they ascended, they do not descend? And one can say: For instance, where there is an interposition between the animal and the pavement of the courtyard. And if you say: And how does [the verse] exclude these three disqualified [offerings]? But one exclusion is needed for an animal that copulated with a person (rova) or was copulated with by a person (nirba), and for all those [disqualifications] regarding which Rabbi Shimon concedes that if they ascended, they must descend! And one can say: [An offering that was] slaughtered at night and [one] whose blood went out are both excluded from a single exclusion, as they are of equal weight. And if you say: [Regarding] Most Holy Sacrifices that one slaughtered in the south [of the courtyard], where [the Gemara] says at the beginning of Me'ilah (daf 2b) that according to Rabbi Yehuda, all agree that [if it ascended,] it must descend — why? Behold, there is no fourth exclusion! And according to Rabbi Shimon as well, according to Rava who says that it must descend: Is its disqualification not [one that occurred] in the sacred? For behold, it has [a precedent for] validity in [the case of] offerings of lesser sanctity, which are valid in the south; as I will explain, wherever it has validity somewhere [in sacrificial law], it is termed "their disqualification occurred in the sacred"! And one can say: Slaughter in the south is akin to slaughter outside [the courtyard], and it is considered as though he strangled them, as [the Gemara] says there according to Rabbi Shimon.

Tosafot on Niddah 40a:1:1.hebrew: יוצא דופן - ממקום שמזרעת. ואם תאמר: למה לי קרא? נילף לידה לידה מבכור, כדילפינן לענין קדשים בסמוך. וי"ל, דאי לאו קרא, הוה דרשינן מתלד לרבות יוצא דופן, כדדריש ר"ש:
Tosafot on Niddah 40a:1:1.english: [An offspring born by] caesarean section - [The Rabbis derive that this is excluded because birth must be] from the place where she conceives (she-mazra'at). And if you say: Why do I need a verse [to teach this]? Let us derive [it via the verbal analogy of] "birth" [from] "birth" from a firstborn (bekhor), just as we derive regarding consecrated animals nearby! And it can be answered that were it not for the verse, we would have expounded from [the word] "teled" to include [an offspring born by] caesarean section, as Rabbi Shimon expounds.

Tosafot on Niddah 40a:5:1.hebrew: כעין שהזריעה - פרש"י: ולרבנן לא צריך קרא, דהא סברי בהמפלת (לעיל נדה כו.) דרובן אינם נימוקים. ומיהו, איצטריך להיכא דהושיטה חיה ידה במעי אשה ומעכב את הולד, דטמאה לרבנן. וי"ל, דתרתי ש"מ:
Tosafot on Niddah 40a:5:1.english: [Something that] resembles what she emitted as seed - Rashi explained that according to the Rabbis, a verse is not needed [to teach this], for they maintain in [the chapter of] HaMapelet (above, 26a) that most [fetuses] do not dissolve [and therefore it is presumed that an intact fetus emerged]. However, [a verse] would be needed for [a case] where a midwife reached her hand into a woman's womb and crushed [or: held back] the fetus, where she [the mother] is impure according to the Rabbis. And one can say that two [teachings] are derived from it [the verse].
